text:
Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after court ruling
- Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off
- Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco
Senegal have been restored as the Africa Cup of Nations champions after a ruling by the court of arbitration for sport (Cas).
Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in a chaotic Afcon final in January but the result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (Caf).
Senegal appealed and on Tuesday Cas published the verdict of its panel of three judges.
Senegal beat Morocco in Rabat after causing a 15-minute delay in play when they walked off in protest at Morocco being awarded a penalty in the last minute of normal time.
Senegal’s star forward Sadio Mané helped to persuade his team to return as tensions rose in the stadium and when the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, restarted the game, Morocco’s Brahim Diaz had his penalty saved. Senegal won with a Pape Gueye goal in extra time.
Football’s laws state that referee decisions are final but Caf appeal judges cited Afcon tournament regulations that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”.
The Cas judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing. Cas verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland’s supreme court, though only on limited procedural grounds.
More than $1m (£770,000) in fines were imposed by Caf disciplinary judges on the two federations, players and Senegal’s then coach, Pape Thiaw.
